title: Vesper and the Summit
premise: Marguerite Marchetti, a salvage diver haunted by a dive that killed her brother, is hired by her old rival Tomas Reyes to reach a navy-sealed wreck before the monsoon — six tides away. As the crew races the fleet and the storm, Marguerite discovers the wreck holds evidence that her brother's death was no accident, and that Tomas was there. In the climax she must choose between loyalty to her crew and exposing the truth; she surfaces with the proof, lets Tomas face the inquiry, and finally buries her brother's memory on her own terms.
about_author: C. M. Okonkwo is a former merchant marine who spent a decade diving wrecks off West African and Southeast Asian coasts before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people whose pasts refuse to stay submerged.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Working a wreck the navy won't discuss, she receives Tomas Reyes's offer: a sealed contract, a shared secret, and a deadline measured in tides before monsoon landfall. She takes the job against her crew's unease. Emotional beat: restless ambition masking dread — she recognizes the coordinates from the dive that killed her brother.

chapters.title: The Fleet at Her Heels
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Marguerite and deckhand Suri. The crew races a rival salvage fleet through reef channels, sabotaged gear, and a near-drowning that forces Marguerite to trust Tomas again. Suri finds an old manifest suggesting the wreck was scuttled deliberately. Emotional beat: loyalty fraying as suspicion spreads through the crew.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Inside the wreck she finds her brother's dive log — and proof Tomas cut his line during the fatal dive years ago. The fleet arrives; a confrontation in the flooding hull leaves Tomas trapped and begging for rescue as the monsoon's first squall hits. Emotional beat: fury and grief colliding with the diver's code that you never leave anyone below.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, closing with Suri. She saves Tomas, then turns his own confession over to the maritime inquiry rather than burying it for the crew's payday. The crew stands by her; the storm breaks over the harbor as she scatters her brother's effects at sea. Emotional beat: hard-won peace — truth costs everything but buys back her identity.
